briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for September 18, 2026. Today's domestic and international climate-related news clearly illustrates the intensification of global disasters, alongside various countries' efforts to address climate change, and the persistent challenges that remain.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensification of Global Disasters and Threats Triggered by Climate Change
sections.content: Recently, the severity of disasters triggered by climate change has become increasingly prominent worldwide. In particular, analyses continue to suggest that glacier and rock collapses due to climate change have caused fatal floods in the Nepal-China border region [5, 7, 39, 43, 47, 48, 50, 54, 57, 59, 63, 66], and Nepal plans to claim millions of dollars from the UN Climate Disaster Fund to respond to such disasters [37, 63]. Furthermore, record-breaking heatwaves pose a severe threat to health, with two out of three Americans recognizing that climate change increases heat-related illnesses [41, 42, 55]. In China, extreme rainfall is causing disproportionate risks to agriculture [46, 62], and domestically, the widespread impacts of climate change are materializing, including an increased risk of complex forest disasters such as large-scale wildfires and landslides [1].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Domestically, active efforts are underway to implement carbon neutrality and transition to renewable energy in response to the climate crisis. Various local governments, including Hamyang-gun, Seongbuk-gu, and Cheonan-si, are encouraging citizen participation through carbon neutrality point systems, practical campaigns, and tree-planting events [8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13]. Innovations in the industrial sector are also being explored, such as the utilization of fuel cells in AI data centers [14] and the carbon-neutral transition of the shipbuilding and shipping industries [16]. In particular, the government is operating an inter-ministerial task force to pioneer an era of 100GW renewable energy and is striving to resolve site and grid bottlenecks by implementing seasonal transmission capacity pilot projects [20, 21, 22, 30, 31]. Region-based efforts to expand renewable energy are also continuing, including the successful conclusion of the Saemangeum Clean Energy Expo [27, 28] and the promotion of priority grid connection for rural solar power [23].

sections.title: 🌱 International Cooperation and Innovation Efforts in Response to the Climate Crisis
sections.content: International cooperation and innovation efforts through climate change research are also noteworthy. KOICA is providing international support by investing 64.9 billion Korean Won in Ethiopia's urban climate crisis response [4], and Ethiopia is actively demonstrating climate change adaptation and mitigation efforts, such as planting 50 billion trees by 2030 through its 'Green Legacy Initiative' [71]. Korea and the International Energy Agency (IEA) are advancing the 'RISE ASIA' initiative to bolster energy security and climate crisis response in Asia [26], and the UN has introduced new tools to enhance tracking of non-party climate actions [61]. Domestically, the Gangwon Provincial Forest Science Research Institute held a working-level consultation meeting for forest research institutions to discuss climate change research cooperation [2], and Kyushu University in Japan is developing land-based seaweed farming technology [3], among other diverse research efforts underway to address climate change.

sections.title: ⚠️ Persistent Climate Vulnerabilities and Policy Challenges
sections.content: However, many challenges and vulnerabilities still exist in responding to the climate crisis. The direct economic impacts of climate change are evident, such as the rebound in domestic producer prices in August due to heatwaves and rising oil prices [35]. The importance of international investment and policy support is highlighted, as financial flows to Africa's renewable energy sector are limited by 'national credit ceilings' [32]. Experts warn that the grand energy transition could falter if 'grassroots renewable energy' is excluded from the unified contract market in 2027 [19]. News that the Amazon rainforest is being pushed to the brink by El Niño, climate change, and crime [56, 58] reminds us of the vulnerability of global ecosystems. Amidst these circumstances, calls are growing for the UK to commit to achieving net-zero by 2050 [65, 68], and the 'Climate Justice March' [34] scheduled for September 19 will serve as an important platform to urge citizen action.

briefing.closing: As we have reviewed in today's briefing, the threat of climate change is intensifying, but diverse efforts are underway both domestically and internationally to overcome it. This is a time that calls for sustained attention and action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
